newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish lower.

text.p: U.S. Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished lower after spending a quiet session trading in narrow ranges.
December meandered on both sides of psychologically key 700.00 and closed below that level and at the lowest price for the week.
A drop in the latest U.S. weekly housing claims sparked worries of wage-inflation that plagued Treasury bonds during the session and spilled into stock indices, traders said.
Initial claims fell to 319,000 in the week ended October 5 from a revised 341,000 in the previous week.
December S&Ps fell early, recovered midmorning after quality buying developed near the lows, then drifted back into negative territory as the T-bond extended its decline.
Traders tied choppy action to nervousness after the run to all-time highs in December S&Ps and before key data due on Friday.

September producer prices and September retail sales will be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT on Friday. PPI was forecast to rise 0.3 percent, with the core rate excluding food and energy seen up 0.2 percent, and retail sales were seen up 0.2 percent overall and up 0.3 percent excluding autos.

Some traders downplayed the weak S&P 500 futures close, saying a pause was healthy after such a steep rally. December S&Ps have gained more than 20.0 points from low to high in October, leaving plenty of players happy to take some profits at these levels, traders said.

"Big deal," one S&P broker said of the weak S&P closes on Wednesday and Thursday. "They couldn't even put anything together on the downside after the bonds closed. There was just no followthrough," he said.
"I think they held up pretty well on the day," he added.
Traders pegged support at 697.35, last Friday's low, and then at 696.00.

December S&Ps closed down 2.10 points at 698.40, KBT Value lines lost 0.90 points to 645.90, new composites lost 0.60 points to 372.35, Nikkei 225 rose 90.0 to 20,985, Midcap 400s were up 0.90 at 245.00, and Nasdaq 100s lost 4.50 points at 758.25. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
